observation.visible_scene: A clear, faceted glass tumbler packed with several irregular ice cubes (some protruding above the rim) stands centered on a reflective tabletop against a smooth, neutral gray gradient background. The glass and its mirror-like reflection at the bottom edge remain in the same screen position throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The ice cubes and the glass show no translation, rotation, or rearrangement from the first to the last frame; the pile geometry (top cube above the rim, central tilted cube, left and right cubes) is constant, indicating a static interval.

Only very subtle, localized changes occur on the glass surface: small bright specular spots / short drip-like marks near the left and right edges of the bowl appear in some frames and fade in others (e.g. a dot on the right edge early on, a thin streak on the left edge mid-clip).
A faint, slow variation in the overall brightness/soft banding of the gray background is perceptible between frames, without any shift of the glass's position relative to the frame edges.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ice is actively melting or the surface is condensing (the excerpt is too short and the changes too subtle to confirm an ongoing phase change versus mere highlight flicker).
Any settling of the cubes before t=0 or any motion after the last frame.
The cause of the small edge highlights (droplets running down vs. moving specular reflections).
uncertain_details: The background brightness drift cannot be confidently attributed to camera movement versus a lighting change, since the backdrop is a featureless gradient; the glass's fixed framing argues against a pan.
The appearance/disappearance of the tiny edge marks is at the limit of visibility and may be noise rather than physical droplets.
